# Extract Demo B's cross-window gesture driver

## Context

This is the gesture phase already planned by #15614. Phase 1's staging extraction shipped through #15616 / #15617. The current source is `examples/dashboard/crossWindow/DemoBWorkspace.mjs`, not the old app path; it still mixes 4,406 lines of host ownership and demo choreography. The [current seam map](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/15614#issuecomment-6693132722) and [Euclid's peer read](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/15614#issuecomment-6688649212) identify a separable next responsibility.

## The Problem

The demo's cross-window gesture driver, source probe, readiness/cancellation reads and witness receipts occupy roughly 900 lines inside the workspace. Readers changing the host still have to navigate this choreography, although it supports only the existing Workbench-to-first-popup demonstration. The parent’s broader host, keyboard and perspective maintenance remains open; moving this responsibility does not complete it.

## The Architectural Reality

At `d9eb21fa5f`, the gesture methods run at lines 1762–2683. The stage facade `positionCrossWindowStage` at 2152–2154 is inside that textual interval but belongs with the existing stage composition. `describeCrossWindowChromeMismatch` at 101–137 is an outside-range dependency with an existing named export consumed by unit tests.

Stats, context, settlement resolver and generation stay host-owned and live. The executor replaces `crossWindowStats`; commit, native admission, disconnect, cancellation and destruction consume it outside this range. A captured construction snapshot or second store would change the contract.

`src/core/Base.mjs#destroy` removes writable instance fields before delayed work can resume. A separately owned driver handle could therefore disappear before cleanup calls the host's probe-restoration method. `src/Neo.mjs#applyMixins` copies prototype methods; `TopologySeams`, already mixed into this host, is the same-owner behavior precedent. Mixin methods overwrite colliding class methods, so the executor must not reuse the host facade's name.

Design authority: #15614's operator-directed maintenance outcome, preserving existing facades and behavior. The docking design record §2.3 permits this per-host stage composition; adopting the normative Workspace superclass is not a prerequisite.

## The Fix

Add `examples/dashboard/crossWindow/DemoBCrossWindowGesture.mjs` as a registered, state-free `Neo.core.Base` mixin. Move the gesture/probe/cancellation methods there as prototype methods. Keep `executeCrossWindowStep(step, options)` on the workspace and delegate to a distinctly named internal runner through the host's normal method dispatch, passing the existing static semantic workspace IDs. Preserve `viaDesktop = roundTrip` and every existing receipt/refusal.

All internal calls continue resolving current host methods, including wrappers installed after construction. Keep the stage facade and semantic commit/native lifecycle ownership on the host. Preserve or re-export the existing named chrome helper. Delete the moved implementations from the workspace rather than leaving a second copy.

Placement: the existing Body example's `crossWindow/` directory, beside `DemoBCrossWindowStage.mjs`; not `src/dashboard/`, because the Workbench/first-popup choreography is demo-specific. The Engine's Structural Inventory and docking ADR were read; this adds no directory or generic subsystem. The new module has class/method JSDoc explaining ownership rather than historical ticket narration.

## Contract Ledger

| Surface | Authority | Preserved behavior | Refusal / fallback | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `executeCrossWindowStep(step, options)` | Existing host method and TourRunner consumer | Same options, promise and receipt shape; Workbench → first popup only; current host method dispatch | Same unsupported-step, missing-pane and runtime error receipts | TourRunner + DemoBWorkspace units; native transfer/round-trip/cancel |
| Probe/readiness/cancel methods | Current host implementations | Host-live stats and context; host timeout/destruction guards; own/inherited source method restoration | An intervening replacement is not overwritten; delayed cleanup remains callable after destruction | Focused lifecycle and wrapper tests |
| Stage and semantic commit facades | Existing `DemoBCrossWindowStage` and host methods | `positionCrossWindowStage`, `openCrossWindowStage`, `adoptCommittedTransferPair` and commit ownership remain host-side and wrappable | Existing cancellation/settlement behavior | Projection-before-open and adoption/retirement ordering controls |
| Named chrome helper | Existing import from DemoBWorkspace | Same exported function and result shape even if implementation moves | Existing mismatch diagnostics | Existing unit imports and native receipt |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The gesture/probe/cancellation implementation has one demo-local owner; the workspace removes it and retains its public entry point. No new driver instance, callback bundle or state store is introduced.
- [ ] Existing method signatures/options, result shapes, dynamic facade wrappers and named chrome-helper import remain valid. The 104-case DemoBWorkspace/TourRunner baseline passes without weakening its assertions.
- [ ] Focused tests cover source-probe own/inherited restoration, an intervening replacement, live stats after replacement, and cleanup after destruction. Cancellation retains Escape-before-mouseup ordering and cannot add a semantic commit.
- [ ] The existing native cross-window transfer, desktop round trip and Escape cancellation journeys pass, preserving pane identity and document outcomes; the third-claimant stage remains independent. State headed/native evidence separately from unit and hosted CI evidence.
- [ ] The full unit suite and affected existing E2E controls pass. No changes to generic Dock protocols, stage/native ownership, perspective behavior or the tour script; no retired pointer-park/conversion machinery is restored.
- [ ] New/changed methods carry accurate JSDoc and summaries. The PR reports the removed workspace code and retained ownership, and leaves #15614 open for its other phases.

## Out of Scope

Workspace superclass adoption, the remaining host/keyboard/perspective phases, new gesture targets, changing timing/receipt thresholds, Engine collaborator rewrites, film production, and the retired vessel-conversion witnesses.

## Avoided Traps

Do not reproduce the old callback-factory prescription or instantiate a new state owner just to shorten the file. Do not capture host methods or stats at construction. Do not move `positionCrossWindowStage` because it lies between the gesture methods. Do not treat a mixin as a wrapper that leaves overridden host methods intact: use distinct internal runner naming. Preserve the actual assertion contracts from the later receipt and pointer-park corrections.
